newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan opposition takes key Taleban town.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition takes key Taleban town.

text.p: Opposition forces on Friday captured the strategic town of Jabal-os-Siraj in Afghanistan's Parwan province from Taleban Islamic militia, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoting its sources in Afghanistan said forces loyal to guerrilla commander Ahmad Shah Masood took the town after heavy fighting and were now clashing with Taleban forces on the way to Charikar to the south.
Jabal-os-Siraj lies on the main highway from Kabul to north Afghanistan, which Taleban forces have been trying to secure to link up with the main northern town of Mazar-i-Sharif.
Masood's fighters began attacking Taleban positions in the area on Thursday after the Taleban were ousted from newly captured Mazar-i-Sharif by local ethnic Uzbek forces and Shi'ite Moslem militia.

Sources in Masood's Jamiat-i-Islami faction had said on Thursday that his forces had taken three towns including Jabal-os-Siraj in surprise attacks earlier on that day, but a Taleban spokesman dismissed the claim and said some areas taken by the opposition were recaptured.
